channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Supreme Audit Chamber launches probe into Ministry of Defense
item.description: Kazakhstan's Supreme Audit Chamber has initiated an audit of the Ministry of Defense. The specific details and scope of the audit were not immediately disclosed.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev posthumously awards soldiers who died in Caspian Sea incident
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has posthumously awarded state honors to military personnel who died during a training exercise in the Mangystau region. The soldiers were part of military unit 29011.

item.title: President Tokayev posthumously awards medals to soldiers fallen in Caspian Sea exercise
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has posthumously awarded state medals to soldiers who died during a training exercise in the Mangystau region. The soldiers were from military unit 29011.

item.title: President posthumously awards soldiers who died in Mangystau region
item.description: The President has posthumously awarded military personnel who died in the Mangystau region. All of them were from military unit 29011. Awards included the "Aibyn" Order of II and III degrees.

item.title: Kazakh President posthumously awards medals to soldiers lost in exercises
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has posthumously awarded state honors to soldiers who died during military exercises in the Mangystau region. The awards recognize their courage and selflessness in fulfilling their military duty. Several soldiers received the "Ayby" order of the II and III degrees.

item.title: Supreme Audit Chamber to audit Ministry of Defense's budget spending efficiency
item.description: The Supreme Audit Chamber has announced an audit into the Ministry of Defense's efficiency in using budget funds. The audit will also assess the material and technical support provided to military units. This initiative aims to ensure effective resource allocation within the defense sector.

item.title: Over 60 individuals defrauded in Bukhara using malicious APK files
item.description: Authorities in Bukhara have arrested individuals suspected of stealing money from over 60 people using malicious APK files. The criminal scheme was reportedly orchestrated by a young individual under 20 from the Samarkand region and their accomplices in various areas.

item.title: 14 servicemen posthumously awarded 'Aybyn' orders after Caspian Sea exercise tragedy
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has posthumously awarded state honors, including the 'Aybyn' order, to 14 servicemen who died during naval exercises in the Caspian Sea. The soldiers were swept out to sea due to severe weather conditions. Three servicemen were rescued, but 14 perished.

item.title: Russia and US Oppose Human Control Over Military AI
item.description: Russia and the United States have agreed to remove restrictions on the use of artificial intelligence in armed conflict during UN negotiations in Geneva. Both nations worked to soften proposed safety measures, removing requirements for human verification of AI-targeted objectives and ethical considerations.

item.title: Tokayev Appoints New Defense Minister Following Military Exercise Tragedy
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has appointed Aidarbek Myrzakhmetov as the new Minister of Defense. This follows the dismissal of the previous minister, Daulet Kosek, after 14 servicemen died during military exercises in the Caspian Sea due to adverse weather conditions.

item.title: Patrol Officers Detain Man with Photos of Drug Stash Locations in Almaty
item.description: Patrol officers in Almaty have detained a 33-year-old man who was allegedly taking photos of drug stash locations to report to his handler. Police have opened a criminal case and arrested the suspect, aiming to uncover the full drug distribution network.

item.title: Tokayev Appoints Aidarbekov New Defense Minister of Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has appointed Aidarbekov as the new Minister of Defense, according to Akorda. Previously, Aidarbekov commanded the Special Operations Forces and was awarded the "Aibyn" Order of II degree.

item.title: Aidarbekov Appointed Minister of Defense
item.description: Aidarbekov has been appointed Minister of Defense. Previously, he commanded the Special Operations Forces.

item.title: Uzbek Official Reacts to Child Sexual Assault Case, Proposes Stricter Penalties
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, expressed outrage over the sexual assault of a 5-year-old girl by a kindergarten employee in Namangan. She announced plans to amend legislation to impose maximum penalties, potentially including the death penalty, for such heinous crimes. Those responsible for negligence will also be punished.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Labor Market Needs Skilled Workers and Service Professionals
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor estimates a need for 2.9 million workers by 2035, with a focus on skilled trades, services, and agriculture. Currently, 42.3% of vacancies are in these sectors. The government aims to increase quality jobs to 3.8 million by 2029.

item.title: Mobile Checkpoints Deployed in Karaganda Region to Combat Livestock Theft
item.description: Police in Kazakhstan's Karaganda region have set up 19 mobile checkpoints on major roads to prevent livestock theft ahead of the autumn slaughter season. The checkpoints, operational since September 25, aim to detect stolen animals and meat being transported illegally. Last year, 46 stolen horses were recovered.

item.title: Seven Ministry Buildings in Tashkent Sold for 868.8 Billion Soums
item.description: Seven ministry and agency buildings in Tashkent have been sold for 868.8 billion Uzbek soums. An additional 11 properties are listed for sale, with preparations underway for the sale of 20 more. This is part of a privatization effort.

item.title: 45 Criminal Cases Against CSTO Members Reach Court
item.description: A total of 45 criminal cases involving members of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) have proceeded to court. The specific nature of the charges or the countries involved were not detailed in the report.

item.title: Kazakhstan Interior Ministry Reports 45 Criminal Cases Sent to Court This Year
item.description: Kazakhstan's Interior Ministry has sent 45 cases involving organized criminal groups to court this year. Sentences range up to 17 years imprisonment for various offenses including theft, fraud, drug trafficking, and extortion across Karaganda, Almaty, Astana, and Kyzylorda regions.

item.title: Two young women arrested and detained for five days for using profanity on TikTok live stream
item.description: Two young women in Almaty were administratively detained for five days for using profanity during a TikTok live stream. Their identities were confirmed after a video of the incident circulated online. Police reminded users that social media is not a lawless zone.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Dismisses Defense Minister After Naval Incident
item.description: Kazakhstan's president has dismissed the defense minister following an incident in the Caspian Sea. The decision came after 17 servicemen drowned, with 14 fatalities reported. The specific circumstances leading to the dismissal were linked to this tragic event.

item.title: Tokayev Congratulates Turkmenistan on 35th Independence Anniversary
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev congratulated the leadership and people of Turkmenistan on their 35th Independence Day. He acknowledged Turkmenistan's achievements in socio-economic development and strengthening its international standing. Kazakhstan values its friendly relations with Turkmenistan and cooperation.

item.title: Ruble Falls Against Somoni, Yuan Rises Amidst Currency Fluctuations
item.description: The Russian ruble has fallen to nearly 10 Tajik somoni, while the Chinese yuan has strengthened. This shift in currency exchange rates over the past three months negatively impacts the income of labor migrants. Further details on the currency changes are available.

item.title: Kazakhstan: 45 Organized Crime Cases Prosecuted Since Start of 2026
item.description: Since the beginning of 2026, Kazakhstan has sent 45 criminal cases against organized crime group members to court, according to Polisia.kz. Sentences have been handed down in several cases, involving charges from property theft to drug trafficking and vehicle fraud.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Minister of Defense Dauren Kosanov Dismissed from Post
item.description: Dauren Kosanov has been relieved of his duties as Minister of Defense of the Republic of Kazakhstan. He had held the position since June 8, 2025. Kosanov's career includes various command roles within the Kazakh Air Defense Forces.

item.title: CSTO Military Contingents from Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan Deployed to Russia
item.description: Military contingents from Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan participating in CSTO exercises have been redeployed to the Russian Federation. The exercises, including 'Interaction-2026', 'Search-2026', and 'Echelon-2026', are focused on collective security and operational readiness.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev congratulates Turkmenistan on Independence Day
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev sent congratulations to Turkmenistan's President Serdar Berdimuhamedov and National Leader Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov on the 35th anniversary of Turkmenistan's independence. He noted Turkmenistan's achievements and strong international standing.

item.title: Lavrov: Europe Hinders Ukraine Peace Talks, Russia Will Achieve Goals
item.description: Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov stated at the UN General Assembly that Europe is doing everything possible to disrupt negotiations between Russia and Ukraine. He asserted that Moscow will achieve all its objectives in the conflict. The statement suggests European actions are obstructing peace talks.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Approves Real Estate Self-Exclusion Bill, Tightens Migration Policy
item.description: Kyrgyz lawmakers approved a bill allowing citizens to self-exclude from real estate transactions to prevent fraud. The government also plans stricter migration checks, noting no foreign workers in the service sector are legally employed. The ADB maintained its economic growth forecast for Kyrgyzstan at 8.9% for 2026 and 8.4% for 2027.

item.title: Uzbek-born man extradited to US on terrorism financing charges
item.description: Davud Ansariy, an Uzbek and naturalized US citizen, was extradited from Tbilisi to New York to face charges of supporting ISIS and Jabhat al-Nusra. The US Justice Department reports he managed a network that raised funds and organized travel for individuals intending to fight for these groups.

item.title: Turkmenistan Celebrates 35 Years of Independence with International Recognition
item.description: Turkmenistan marks 35 years of independence, achieving significant political and economic successes and gaining international prestige. The nation's neutrality policy, recognized by the UN, contributes to its growing global standing. Close neighborly relations are expected to evolve into effective strategic partnerships.

item.title: Turkmenistan Marks 35 Years of Independence with Cultural Concert
item.description: A celebratory concert by cultural and art masters marked Turkmenistan's 35th anniversary of independence in Ashgabat. President Serdar Berdimuhamedow attended the event, highlighting the nation's significant achievements and its transformation into a center for peace and cooperation. The country's progress is attributed to its independence.

item.title: Turkmenistan Grants Residency Permits to Foreign Citizens on Humanitarian Grounds
item.description: Turkmenistan has issued residency permits to foreign citizens living permanently in the country, based on a humanitarian decree signed by President Serdar Berdimuhamedow. This event underscores the nation's commitment to humanitarian principles and strengthens unity. Those receiving permits expressed gratitude to the President and Arkadag.

item.title: Iran and Afghanistan Expand Transit Cooperation, Including Chabahar Port Use
item.description: Iran's chargé d'affaires in Kabul, Ali Reza Bigdeli, announced expanded transit and logistics cooperation with Afghanistan, focusing on Chabahar and Bandar Abbas ports. Afghanistan has appointed a representative to follow up on Chabahar port matters, with ongoing talks. Chabahar port facilitates Afghan goods to international waters and markets, connecting Afghanistan and Central Asia to India.

item.title: Turkmenistan President Pardons 1,054 Individuals on Independence Day
item.description: Turkmenistan's President Serdar Berdimuhamedow signed a decree pardoning 1,054 individuals on the occasion of the country's 35th Independence Day on September 25. State media reported the pardon but did not specify the names or crimes of those released. It remains unclear if political prisoners were included. The decree also lifts additional penalties.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election Set for Wednesday, January 27, 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's presidential election will be held on Wednesday, January 27, 2027, for the first time under new legislation. The government plans to provide a paid day off for voters. The election process will utilize digital systems for faster results and reduced error risks.

item.title: Turkmenistan's Education System Faces Challenges Amidst Reforms
item.description: A recent meeting of the Halk Maslahaty focused on youth and education reform, proposing a state program for talented youth. However, reports highlight issues in schools, including a mass brawl among 11th graders resulting in injuries and a teacher assaulting a younger student. These incidents are reportedly not uncommon.

item.title: Erdogan criticizes global system, states war criminals belong in court, not UN
item.description: Turkish President Erdogan stated that the modern global system is in crisis regarding legality and justice. He condemned the prevailing principle of "might makes right" in international relations. Erdogan asserted that war criminals belong in the courtroom, not on UN platforms.

item.title: Activists call for international recognition of "Hazara genocide" in Afghanistan
item.description: The Hazara Diaspora Network and other activists have called for the mass killings of Hazaras between 1891-1893 to be recognized as genocide. Citing the 1948 UN Convention, they urge international action against ongoing discrimination, property seizures, and forced displacement in Afghanistan.

item.title: Taliban's double standard: Foreign women escorted in parks, Afghan women whipped
item.description: Taliban authorities reportedly escort foreign women in Afghan parks while whipping local women who attempt to enter. This double standard, observed at sites like Band-e Amir, highlights the group's disregard for its own rules and the severe restrictions faced by Afghan women and girls.
